findings.summary: Every review and baseline run now checks out into the same fixed path, `scratchpad/eddy-tree`, so a second eddy run started while one is still going checks out its own commit over the first one's tree and deletes the first one's files.
findings.detail: Before this change `snapshot` made a separate worktree for each commit (`scratchpad/eddy-trees/<sha>`), so two reviews of different commits never touched each other's files. Now `snapshot` calls `checkout_at(".", TREE, sha)`, which runs `checkout --force`, then `reset --hard`, then `clean -ffdx` on the one shared tree. The `eddy-review` mise task wraps only reviews that run code in `scripts/exclusive.sh`. A `--no-run` review and `tools/baseline.wado` take no lock, so they can run alongside another review. When they do, the later one moves the shared tree to its commit while the earlier reviewer is still reading it. The earlier reviewer then reads, greps and builds the wrong commit. Its Write'd tests are removed by `clean -ffdx`, and its reporter's repro re-run runs against the wrong commit. The SCIP index directory (`scratchpad/eddy-tree-index`) is shared the same way. I ran `checkout_at`'s git steps through node in a scratch repository, since the sandbox blocks git under `wado test`. I checked out commit A, wrote a file into the tree, then checked out B. The 'review of A' then read B's file contents, and the file it had written was gone (`f = B`, `repro.rs` exists: false).

description = "Review this branch with Eddy; arguments go to it (`--no-run` keeps it from building and running the code)"
run = """
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
wado="$(scripts/dev-bin.sh --path wado)"
case " $* " in
    *" --no-run "*) set -- "$wado" run package-eddy/src/main.wado -- "$@" ;;
    # The reviewer builds with cargo, which would starve a test run and be
    # starved by it. `wado run` refuses a grant of a path that does not exist,
    # so the homes are granted only to a review that runs cargo or mise, and
    # mise's binary and data directory only where they exist.
    *)
        set -- package-eddy/src/main.wado -- "$@"
        for granted in "${MISE_DATA_DIR:-$HOME/.local/share/mise}" "$(command -v mise)"; do
            if [ -e "$granted" ]; then set -- --process-read "$granted" "$@"; fi
        done
        set -- ./scripts/exclusive.sh test "$wado" run \
            --process-read "${CARGO_HOME:-$HOME/.cargo}" --process-read "${RUSTUP_HOME:-$HOME/.rustup}" "$@"
        ;;
esac
# A child of `wado run` may run only a system-wide program, and mise's `rg`
# shim is ahead of `/usr/bin/rg` on PATH otherwise. Set after `wado` is built,
# which must find the toolchain mise installs.
PATH="/usr/bin:$PATH" exec "$@"
"""
